programs.name: Agency Multifamily (Fannie Mae DUS and Freddie Mac Optigo)
programs.description: Fannie Mae DUS and Freddie Mac Optigo programs for stabilized market-rate, workforce, and LIHTC multifamily. The most competitive execution for stabilized multifamily in most markets.
typical_stack: Fannie Mae DUS (delegated underwriting and servicing) 10-year fixed permanent
Freddie Mac Optigo (Target, SBL, Green Advantage, TAH) permanent
Agency green bond programs for energy-efficient properties
Fannie MAH and Freddie TAH for LIHTC and workforce affordable

key_features.rate_environment_2026: 10-year fixed 5.5 to 6.5 percent depending on leverage and asset profile
key_features.typical_ltv: 70 to 80 percent for market-rate, higher for workforce and affordable
key_features.prepayment: Yield maintenance or step-down depending on program
key_features.minimum_deal_size: $1M for SBL, no maximum for standard DUS/Optigo

programs.name: CMBS Multifamily Financing
programs.description: Commercial mortgage-backed securities conduit financing for stabilized multifamily. Most competitive when sponsor wants higher proceeds, non-recourse, and is willing to live within CMBS structure.
typical_stack: Fixed-rate IO-only periods for strong deals
Mezzanine overlay occasionally for aggressive leverage

key_features.rate_environment_2026: Spreads 200 to 300 over 10-year Treasury depending on deal quality
key_features.prepayment: Yield maintenance for first 8 years, open after

programs.name: Multifamily Value-Add Bridge Financing
programs.description: Bridge financing for multifamily value-add business plans: acquire underperforming property, renovate units and common areas, raise rents at turnover, stabilize, refinance into permanent.
typical_stack: Bridge loan from debt fund, mortgage REIT, or specialty bank
Interest reserve sized to carry property during renovation and lease-up
Renovation budget (unit interiors, common areas, exterior)
Exit to agency or CMBS at stabilization

key_features.rate_environment_2026: SOFR + 400 to 650 bps, floor rates common
key_features.typical_ltv_ltc: 75 to 80 percent LTC, 70 to 75 percent of stabilized value
key_features.term: 2 to 3 years with 1 to 2 year extension options
key_features.prepayment: Open after lockout period (typically 12 to 18 months)
key_features.recourse_structure: Typically non-recourse with bad-boy carve-outs; some deals require partial recourse

programs.name: Ground-Up Multifamily Construction Financing
programs.description: Ground-up market-rate multifamily construction financing. Bank construction lenders, debt fund non-bank construction, and life company forward commitments for the permanent take-out.
typical_stack: Construction loan (bank, debt fund, or specialty construction lender)
Life company forward commitment for permanent take-out (when available)
Mezzanine debt or preferred equity for leverage
Sponsor equity and limited partner equity

key_features.rate_environment_2026: SOFR + 275 to 400 bps construction, life co forward 5.25 to 6.25 fixed
key_features.term: 2 to 3 years construction with 1 to 2 year stabilization extension
key_features.recourse_structure: Completion guarantee and recourse common; non-recourse rarer in current market

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.market_notes: LA multifamily features rent stabilization (RSO) on pre-1978 properties, AB 1482 statewide rent control, and high barriers to entry. Market dominated by value-add opportunity on older rent-stabilized stock and ground-up development in growth submarkets.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Agencies very competitive for stabilized; life companies selectively for top-quality. CMBS active for $10M+ stabilized. Debt funds are dominant for value-add bridge given LA's value-add heavy deal flow. Construction lending has tightened but debt fund alternatives available.
cities.submarkets: Koreatown, Hollywood, Silver Lake, Echo Park, DTLA, Culver City, West LA, Sherman Oaks, Van Nuys, Long Beach

cities.name: Phoenix
cities.market_notes: One of the hottest multifamily markets nationally through 2022, moderated in 2023-2024, now stabilizing. Strong in-migration, limited rent control, pro-development regulatory environment. Substantial ground-up supply in recent years has been digested.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Agencies very active and competitive. CMBS strong. Life companies competitive for Class A. Debt funds active for value-add and ground-up. BTR has seen massive capital deployment in Phoenix metro with specialty lenders competing.
cities.submarkets: Downtown Phoenix, Tempe, Scottsdale, Chandler, Gilbert, Mesa, Goodyear, Glendale

cities.name: Dallas
cities.market_notes: DFW is one of the top multifamily markets in the country driven by corporate relocations, population growth, and a pro-development regulatory environment. Both urban core and suburban submarkets have strong deal flow.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Agencies very competitive. CMBS active for $10M+. Life companies aggressive for Class A. Regional Texas banks strong on construction. Debt funds for value-add. BTR lending universe particularly active in DFW.
cities.submarkets: Uptown, Downtown Dallas, Oak Lawn, Deep Ellum, Plano, Frisco, McKinney, Richardson, Addison, Las Colinas

cities.name: Austin
cities.market_notes: Austin experienced dramatic rent growth through 2022 followed by sharp moderation in 2023-2024 due to supply surge. Now finding equilibrium with strong fundamentals and tech-driven demand, though submarket dispersion is significant.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Agencies competitive with some caution on supply-heavy submarkets. CMBS active. Life companies selective. Debt funds for value-add and bridge. Construction lending cautious on supply-constrained underwriting. Ground-up market-rate has moderated.
cities.submarkets: Downtown, East Austin, South Congress, North Loop, Mueller, Cedar Park, Round Rock, Pflugerville

cities.name: Nashville
cities.market_notes: Nashville has been one of the strongest secondary multifamily markets for the past decade. Healthcare, music, and tourism-driven economy with sustained in-migration. Moderating from peak but still growing.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Agencies very competitive. CMBS active. Life companies interested. Regional banks strong on construction. BTR active. Overall a very financeable market with good lender depth.
cities.submarkets: Germantown, The Gulch, East Nashville, Midtown, Green Hills, Brentwood, Franklin, Murfreesboro

cities.name: Denver
cities.market_notes: Denver multifamily has stabilized after strong growth 2018-2022. Mature market with solid fundamentals, though new supply in certain submarkets has pressured rents. Ground-up activity has moderated but selectively active.
cities.active_lender_commentary: Agencies competitive. CMBS active. Life companies selective. Debt funds for value-add. Construction lending cautious on supply-heavy submarkets but available for strong sponsors.
cities.submarkets: LoDo, RiNo, Capitol Hill, Cherry Creek, Highland, Washington Park, Lakewood, Aurora, Boulder
